metadata.title: Dow Investors Chased Tech Swings—While Amgen Quietly Surged 77%

content.text:
Investing.com and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue on some items through the links below.
Investing.com — Sudden reversals in AI chipmakers and mega-cap tech, set off by the leadership shake-up at Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), have kept Dow investors fixated on the next swing. Yet Amgen (NASDAQ:AMGN)—the large-cap biotechnology leader behind osteoporosis drug EVENITY and lung cancer drug IMDELLTRA—has climbed another 2.29% in November to $473.94.
The market is pricing Amgen as a Dow stalwart facing a patent cliff, not as a company whose newest drugs are already outgrowing the old ones. Its six key growth drivers expanded 27% year-over-year last quarter, and the shares have climbed without the headline whiplash.
The market's reading missed what ProPicks AI, the model InvestingPro uses to rank stocks on earnings momentum and financial durability, saw first: it placed Amgen in Dominate the Dow, its themed list of blue-chip Dow leaders, at $320.75, and the stock is up 76.54% since. Amgen is one of ten Dow leaders on that list, and what the other nine share with it is what the test is picking up.
Amgen's moat is breadth: 17 products now annualize above $1 billion in sales, so no single drug decides the year. The six key growth drivers—Repatha, EVENITY, TEZSPIRE, UPLIZNA, rare disease, and oncology—grew a combined 27% year-over-year and now make up over 70% of product sales. A platform that steers the body's own immune cells onto cancer cells stands behind IMDELLTRA and BLINCYTO, and in first-line maintenance small cell lung cancer, IMDELLTRA cut the risk of death by 58% against IMFINZI alone, the comparison treatment.
Third-quarter results proved that the newer drugs are carrying the growth. Adjusted EPS of $6.45 beat consensus by $0.69, and revenue of $10.4 billion, up 8% year-over-year, topped estimates by $340 million. UPLIZNA surged 191% to $451 million, Repatha climbed 37% to $1.1 billion, EVENITY rose 39% to $751 million, and IMDELLTRA more than doubled to $406 million. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to $38.9 billion to $39.7 billion in revenue and $22.90 to $23.70 in non-GAAP EPS.
Cash followed profit. Non-GAAP operating margin held at 47% and quarterly free cash flow reached $3.7 billion, funding research and development spending up 11% year-over-year, a 6% dividend increase to $2.52 per share that extends a 16-year growth streak, and share repurchases capped at $3 billion for 2026.
Wall Street Trails the Price While Fair Value Edges Past It
Wall Street is split. Piper Sandler rates Amgen a Buy at $542, with Goldman Sachs at $536 and UBS at $530, while Barclays holds at $430 and Truist at $398. Targets run from $230 to $542 around an average of $435.77, which sits below the $473.94 share price.
InvestingPro's Fair Value of $479.90 per share is more generous: it sits just above the share price and about 10% above the average target.
The main risk is the patent clock. Roughly 67% of revenue faces patent expiration through 2030, including Prolia, Xgeva, Enbrel, and Otezla, with biosimilar competition already intensifying. Debt from the $27.8 billion Horizon Therapeutics acquisition leaves total debt at $54.0 billion, TEPEZZA sales fell 6% to $526 million, and 20 analysts have cut estimates over the past 90 days against only six who raised them. Management also guided for a meaningful sequential rise in fourth-quarter operating expenses.
The shares sit close to the 52-week high of $481.20, and anyone adding Amgen now is weighing broad growth drivers against patent exposure and a heavy debt load, and the Amgen Pro Research Report sets out how far the newer drugs, the obesity pipeline, and the dividend can carry it.
Amgen is replacing aging franchises with new ones faster than the market gives it credit for, and the cash it generates is funding the pipeline that has to carry it past the patent cliff. That durable compounding is what the crowd missed while it chased the swings.
Amgen stays in Dominate the Dow only while it keeps passing the test that put it there, which makes InvestingPro's list a running check on whether the newer drugs are still winning the race against the patent clock.
